newsitem.title: USA: Demeter BioTech says compounds effective.
newsitem.headline: Demeter BioTech says compounds effective.

text.p: Demeter BioTechnologies Ltd said Monday that results from in vitro studies indicate its proprietary compounds could be effective in treating cancer.

Researchers at Duke University Medical Center demonstrated in vitro that a single, low dose of treatment with Demeter's Peptidyl Membrane Interactive Molecule, an anti-cancer molecule, killed 98 percent of the cell line PC-3, a common prostate cancer model, the company said.
The company said the studies also showed the molecule was effective against cells derived from prostate cancer that had spread to the lymph nodes, vertebrate, bone and brain.
Additional studies demonstrated that Peptidyl is effective against other types of cancer cells, including breast, cervical, colon, bladder, melanoma and lung, the company said.
Demeter said more testing will need to be done before human trials can begin.
Demeter designs and develops synthetic molecules for anti-infective and anti-cancer uses.
